title: RTX Spark Ignites Global Celebration as New Windows PCs Arrive
body: RTX Spark Ignites Global Celebration as New Windows PCs Arrive NVIDIA celebrates the arrival of RTX Spark with retail launch events around the world, bringing gamers, creators and AI enthusiasts together for hands-on experiences. October 17, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops are now available, bringing NVIDIA Blackwell RTX graphics, up to 128GB of unified memory and the full NVIDIA AI platform to slim, premium Windows PCs. Starting at $2,399, laptops from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI bring powerful local AI, content creation and gaming capabilities to a portable device, with additional systems on the way. NVIDIA celebrated the launch with events around the world, including one in Berlin, where NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made a surprise appearance. A New Generation of Windows PCs Has Arrived RTX Spark brings decades of NVIDIA accelerated computing innovation into a single superchip, combining an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and NVIDIA Grace CPU with up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and up to 128GB of unified memory. Read more in the press release . RTX Spark Launch Celebrations Light Up Berlin The arrival of RTX Spark brought fans, creators and PC enthusiasts together in Berlin during the Festival of Lights, an annual autumn art festival that transforms the German capital’s most famous landmarks, streets and squares into glowing canvases. This year, the festival featured RTX Spark-themed lighting on the Berlin TV Tower. Berlin sparked something special, indeed. Fans gathered hours ahead in anticipation for the launch celebration at XPERION, the gaming venue inside Saturn at Alexanderplatz, where attendees got hands-on with RTX Spark laptops from leading PC makers, exploring the latest gaming experiences, content-creation workflows and local AI capabilities. Even this Geralt cosplayer waited to get his hands on RTX Spark. The celebration included a special appearance by Huang, who greeted an enthusiastic crowd, passed out popcorn and posed for selfies. He also gave out five personally signed RTX Spark laptops. You get a signed RTX Spark. You get a signed RTX Spark. Berlin held one of six RTX Spark retail launch celebrations worldwide. From San Francisco to Seoul: How the World Welcomed RTX Spark A massive crowd gathered at the JD MALL Shuangjing Store in Beijing to celebrate the highly anticipated launch, enjoying a night of innovation and community connection. Crowds gathered to demo RTX Spark at the Beijing RTX Spark launch party. Attendees at Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı in Istanbul experienced a lively event filled with interactive demonstrations and specialized programming led by local creators. Attendees witnessed local celebrities speak at the RTX Spark launch party in Istanbul. Seoul’s COEX East Lobby transformed into a bustling hub of creativity, hosting an eager crowd for engaging hands-on demos and captivating evening sessions dedicated to gaming and AI. Hands-on demos at the RTX Spark launch party in Seoul. Tech enthusiasts in San Francisco visited the local Best Buy store for an unforgettable morning of hands-on RTX Spark demos, fireside chats with local founders and a special appearance by tech influencer iJustine. Lines were long but lively at the San Francisco RTX Spark launch party. The energy at Muse Garden in Taipei was electric as the local AI community came together for a vibrant evening of music, engaging discussions and incredible product showcases. Incredible atmosphere at the Taipei RTX Spark launch party. Developers and AI enthusiasts can explore NVIDIA-tested recipes, playbooks and resources for running local AI on RTX Spark . Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X . See notice regarding software product information. title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
body:
IMFC Statement Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date Christine Lagarde The President of the European Central Bank SPEECH IMFC Statement Statement by Christine Lagarde, President of the ECB, at the fifty-fourth meeting of the International Monetary and Financial Committee IMF Annual Meetings, 17 October 2026 Introduction The global economy has proven surprisingly resilient in the face of high uncertainty. The conflict in the Middle East continues to expose energy markets to sharp swings. Trade tensions and protectionist measures are weighing on confidence and contributing to a reconfiguration of trade flows. The global economy has held up thanks in part to the rise of artificial intelligence, with investment in technology supporting activity and trade, particularly in economies integrated into technology value chains. Risks nonetheless remain tilted to the downside for growth and to the upside for inflation. A return to an international economic order grounded in openness, predictability and the rule of law would help trade and investment flourish. Economic activity Despite global headwinds and the ongoing energy shock, the euro area economy has so far proved resilient. Growth was broad-based across most euro area countries and sectors in the first half of 2026. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. As the energy shock fades over the medium term, the projections see domestic demand benefitting from a recovery in real income over the medium term, driven by lower energy inflation and a resilient labour market. Rising government spending on infrastructure and defence, complemented by investment in AI and digital technologies, should also support growth. Export growth should pick up on the back of strengthening foreign demand, also driven by AI. The medium-term outlook is surrounded by uncertainty over how intense and long-lasting the Middle East conflict will be, and how the resulting shocks might propagate through the economy. Risks to growth are assessed to be on the downside. Fiscal sustainability remains a crucial anchor for broader economic stability. It is important to maintain sound fiscal policies, including by adhering to fiscal rules, and, where debt is high, to consolidate, re-prioritise spending and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of public finances to rebuild buffers. Governments should strive to ensure that any fiscal response to the energy shock is temporary, targeted and tailored. In addition, policies that strengthen resilience to climate change can improve the economy’s ability to absorb climate-related shocks. These efforts should be complemented by structural policies that promote labour market participation, equip the workforce with the skills needed in an AI-driven economy and facilitate the diffusion of new technologies. Priorities include advancing the savings and investments union, improving access to risk capital and creating better conditions for innovative firms to scale up across the Single Market. Inflation Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. Core inflation increased slightly to 2.5%. The range of underlying inflation measures remained broadly stable in September and wages have so far shown no material response to the energy shock. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation. Headline inflation is expected to decline after the first quarter as energy inflation falls, returning to around target towards the end of 2027. The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside due, in particular, to the Middle East conflict and Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine. A more intense or persistent energy shock could strengthen indirect and second-round effects, resulting in higher and more persistent inflation. Extreme weather could push up food prices. By contrast, a sustainable resolution of geopolitical conflicts, weaker energy pass-through or more risk-averse financial markets could lower inflation. Monetary policy The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. Our interest rate decisions are based on our reaction function, which comprises three criteria: our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, the dynamics of underlying inflation; and the strength of monetary policy transmission. The inflation outlook points to higher inflation ahead, especially in the short term, given the latest developments in energy markets. However, we see no evidence at this stage of significant pass-through of energy prices to other prices and wages, beyond what we have already included in our projections. And while growth has been resilient, financing conditions have tightened, with long-term interest rates rising notably since our last meeting. This will slow growth and reduce pass-through by more than projected in our September exercise. Taking these three criteria together, the energy shock is too large to “look through” but a measured response remains appropriate to keep inflation in check. In setting future policy, we will make a comprehensive assessment of the incoming data based on our reaction function. In July, the Governing Council decided on the operational features and the onboarding process for the enhanced EUREP, the Eurosystem repo facility for central banks that was announced earlier this year. The new facility supports the smooth transmission of monetary policy and reinforces the international role of the euro. More than 30 central banks have expressed interest in EUREP in the past six months. Financial stability Sources of risk and vulnerabilities for euro area financial stability remain high. Continued geopolitical tensions, fiscal challenges and uncertainties around accelerated AI adoption continue to be causes for concern. The widespread concentration of critical third-party service providers introduces single points of failure for both financial and non-financial institutions. New frontier AI models have increased cyber risks and operational vulnerabilities. Euro area banks maintain strong capital and liquidity buffers and robust profitability, together with healthy and stable asset quality. These solid fundamentals should help navigate ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and effectively support lending to the economy. Strengthened prudential regulation and supervision since the global financial crisis has helped leave euro area banks in a strong position to withstand the unfolding economic challenges. Shocks could expose vulnerabilities among non-bank financial intermediaries, notably from concentrated AI-related exposures, amplifying market stress and creating spillovers across financial sectors. Banks’ exposures to non-banks and vulnerable firms could expose funding and credit vulnerabilities. Stress in private credit markets has continued, with private credit funds reporting outflows and reactivating redemption gates. Private market “semi-liquid funds” that allow for redemptions are becoming more prevalent, which could lead to greater liquidity mismatches in the future, but euro area financial institutions have limited direct exposure to private credit. This means, for now, that private credit in isolation is unlikely to be a source of financial instability in the euro area. Payment systems Central bank money must evolve to fulfil the needs of an increasingly digital economy. The Eurosystem is at the forefront of this evolution, bringing the stability and trust of central bank money to digital retail payments and tokenised finance in Europe. In the retail space we are preparing to complement cash with its digital equivalent – the digital euro – for day-to-day payments. The digital euro will further stimulate innovation and competition in retail payments, ensuring that the continued co-existence of public and private solutions underpins Europe’s strategic autonomy in payments. To lay the groundwork for a seamless and secure launch, we will run a 12-month internal pilot in the second half of 2027. Adopting the Regulation on the establishment of the digital euro by the end of 2026 is key to making this possible. In the wholesale space, the Eurosystem is developing new capabilities to ensure that central bank money can settle transactions in the growing market of tokenised assets. Pontes – the Eurosystem’s distributed ledger technology (DLT) solution that went live on 21 September – marks the first step in implementing our strategy to enable the development of a European tokenised ecosystem. This vision will be advanced under the Appia initiative, which aims to deliver a blueprint for this ecosystem based on common standards, shared network infrastructure and European governance. International cooperation We value the work of our global institutions and fora, particularly those that promote global macroeconomic and financial stability. We welcome the recent completion of the three major IMF reviews (Comprehensive Surveillance Review, Financial Sector Assessment Program Review and Review of Program Design and Conditionality), which strengthen the role of the IMF at the centre of the global financial safety net. Climate-related work should remain fully anchored in IMF operations, particularly surveillance. Multilateral efforts to help tackle global imbalances support coordination of domestic action that is required to minimise the risks from disorderly adjustment. The IMF’s analytical work on global imbalances and its improvements to the methodology for assessing external balances provide a strong basis for these efforts. title: Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
body: October 16, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for August 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for September 2026, is scheduled for November 18, 2026. The sum total in August of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $199.8 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $178.5 billion, and net foreign official inflows were $21.3 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in August; their net purchases were $300.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $257.8 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $42.9 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $21.6 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $279.2 billion in August. Foreign residents decreased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $47.8 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $37.8 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s International Financial Networks and Shadow Banking Architecture
body: October 15, 2026 Action Disrupts Iraqi Bank Enabling Iranian Sanctions Evasion and Cuts Off Key Foreign Currency Lifelines WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury disrupted Iran’s efforts to infiltrate the international financial system through an Iraqi bank that also supports Iran’s terrorist proxy militia groups.  By dismantling these institutions—including offshore banks and shadow financiers that have moved hundreds of millions of dollars through shell companies and foreign‑exchange specialists across the Middle East and Asia—Treasury is severing critical revenue streams that sustain Iran’s military and proxy forces. “The noose is tightening around Iran’s economy, and not even Iran’s so-called allies can save it,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The Department of the Treasury will not relent until the Iranian regime’s coffers are empty and every remaining financial lifeline sustaining its war machine has been severed.” In coordination with today’s action, the U.S. Department of State is concurrently designating Cuba-based Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order (E.O.) 14404 for operating in or having operated in the financial services sector of the Cuban economy.  BICSA has provided services to the designated Iran-based Karafarin Bank since at least 2022. These designations, coupled with additional sanctions on Iran’s shadow banking networks, cut off some of the few remaining financial lifelines the regime can access to prop up its failing economy and fund its military.  The designations also expose the regime’s deliberate use of complex offshore structures and front companies to circumvent sanctions and stabilize its economy despite mounting pressure.  Taken together, today’s measures target the core financial architecture that enables Iran to evade international scrutiny and fund its destabilizing regional activities.  Treasury’s action is being taken pursuant to E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including Iran’s financial and petroleum sectors. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  It also expanded secondary sanctions exposure for those who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . Because Iran is already subject to comprehensive U.S. sanctions, it relies on multi-jurisdictional shadow banking networks to generate revenue and transfer funds abroad.  Iran uses these shadow banking networks to launder funds, procure weapons, access U.S. dollar correspondent banking relationships, and bankroll its regional terrorist proxy groups.  These networks rely on financial institutions such as the recently designated Golden Global Bank , and Operation Economic Outcast will continue to identify these banks and remove their access to the U.S. dollar. IRAQI BANK PROVIDING U.S. DOLLAR ACCESS FOR IRAN Iraq-based International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (IDB) provides financial facilitation services and U.S. dollar access for Iran.  IDB has abused its access to the now-dissolved U.S. dollar wire auction and maintains ties to Iranian government entities and Iran-aligned militia groups (IAMGs) in Iraq.  IDB was initially established by Iranian companies to support the Iranian economy and supply Iran with U.S. dollars.  U.S.-designated Bank Melli , which was located next to IDB in Iraq, closed due to U.S. sanctions and transferred its capital to IDB.  IDB uses Iranian capital to conduct business, then collects any profit made and sends it back to Iran in the form of U.S. dollars each month.  The bank’s current leadership received ownership of IDB from a dual-Iranian Iraqi financier working for the U.S.-designated Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps–Qods Force (IRGC-QF).  The financier continues to use his familial relationships to exert influence over the bank. IDB is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. IRANIAN “OFFSHORE” BANKS In addition to establishing correspondent banking relationships with financial institutions in allied countries, the Iranian government has authorized certain banks to operate “ offshore ” in free trade zones.  These Iranian banks have been approved by the Central Bank of Iran and the Supreme National Security Council to conduct their operations using foreign currency to aid sanctions evasion schemes.  Iran-based Jazireh International Bank Company is an Iranian offshore bank affiliated with Bank Mellat, while Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company is an offshore bank affiliated with Bank Shahr. Jazireh International Bank Company and Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. IRANIAN OIL “TRUSTEE” Many of Iran’s key revenue generation streams are corruptly controlled by Iranian regime elites.  These revenue streams include the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani , son of Ali Shamkhani, the late advisor to Iran’s Supreme Leader, and the vast overseas property holdings of Ali Ansari , a key benefactor of Mojtaba Khamenei.  One of the elites controlling Iran’s key revenue streams is Iranian national Sayyed Ruhollah Razavi (Razavi), son-in-law of Iran’s hardline Paydari Front leader and one of the top oil trustees on whom the Iranian regime relies to sell oil and repatriate the revenue. Living in Dubai as one of Iran’s top oil intermediaries, Razavi has worked hand-in-hand with Seyed Naiemaei Badroddin Moosavi , a Hizballah financier and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force facilitator designated on April 15, 2026.  Prior to the U.S. blockade preventing Iranian oil exports, Razavi was responsible for shipping millions of barrels of oil overseas each month on behalf of the National Iranian Oil Company and its subsidiary, Naftiran Intertrade Company.  Razavi has also used his network to move the revenue generated from these oil sales through Iran’s clandestine banking system of shell companies and cash and gold couriers.  These networks move funds through Hong Kong to the UAE and Türkiye where they are converted to gold and cash and then smuggled on Mahan Air flights to Iran and its terrorist proxies around the world.  Razavi is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy. In addition to his overseas work on behalf of Iran, Razavi manages Iran-based companies Tejarat Gostar Atlas Parsian Kish Company and Farzanegan Energy Pars Company , the latter of which is currently developing the Farzanegan Gas Condensate Refinery in Iran’s Bushehr Province.  Tejarat Gostar Atlas Parsian Kish Company and Farzanegan Energy Pars Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Razavi. SHADOW BANKING OPERATIVES Farab Sorough Qeshm Company (FSAQ), an affiliate of Iran’s Shahr Bank, relies on a cadre of foreign exchange experts to process transactions essential to the operations of Iran’s leading oil sales companies and brokers, including the National Iranian Oil Company, Triliance Petrochemical Company, and the military-controlled Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company.  FSAQ employees help to coordinate financial transactions through its rahbar network using shell companies established in Hong Kong and the UAE.  Today, OFAC is designating seven FSAQ employees who have been involved in foreign exchange operations linked to FSAQ: Zhila Mohammadi , Milad Katebi , Amir Sabeti , Nazanin Borji , Fatemeh Vasighi Meraji , Azadeh Abdolalipur , and Farzad Allahyar .  Hong Kong-based Elitesphere Trading Co., Limited , which has been used by FSAQ to move funds through the rahbar network of brokers and front companies in support of Iranian sanctions evasion, is also being designated for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. Zhila Mohammadi, Milad Katebi, Amir Sabeti, Nazanin Borji, Fatemeh Vasighi Meraji, Azadeh Abdolalipur, and Farzad Allahyar are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, FSAQ. Iran-based exchange house Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Partners Qeshm General Partnership (Hosseini Parsa Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Khaled Mohiesnejad , assists the rahbar financial activities of sanctioned Iranian banks alongside Dominican/Iranian national Sadegh Bavi .  Sadegh Bavi, an IRGC-Qods Force facilitator and money launderer who also assists in weapons purchases for Iran, is the owner and general manager of the Bavi General Trading Company LLC , which was previously designated by OFAC for helping coordinate tens of millions of dollars’ worth of payments for front companies operated by the Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co. and Triliance Petrochemical Co. Ltd .  Hosseini Parsa Exchange has a close relationship with Bavi General Trading, which has used Hosseini Parsa Exchange’s official documents and letterhead to carry out its own business operations.  Sadegh Bavi also owns and operates Bavi and Partners Exchange Company , another Iran-based currency exchange house. Iran-based exchange house Soheil and Sorush Najafzadeh and Partners Company (Najafzadeh Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Sorush Najafzadeh , Soheil Najafzadeh , and Mansureh Mirmohammadi , has processed transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of financial transactions for Iranian financial institutions, including entities linked to Bank Mellat and its rahbar, Tejarat Sarir Afrooz Kish .  Iran-based exchange house Abolhasan Jalali and Partners Exchange Company (Jalali Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Abolhassan Jalali and Ensiyeh Mullah Mohammadi , has likewise facilitated tens of millions of dollars’ worth of payments for Iran’s shadow banking networks and sanctioned rahbar entities. Elitesphere Trading Co., Limited, Hosseini Parsa Exchange, Jalali Exchange, Najafzadeh Exchange, Bavi and Partners Exchange Company, Sorush Najafzadeh, Soheil Najafzadeh, Abolhassan Jalali, Ensiyeh Mullah Mohammadi, and Sadegh Bavi are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.  Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Khaled Mohiesnejad are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hosseini Parsa Exchange.  Mansureh Mirmohammadi is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Najafzadeh Exchange. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, and from engaging in conduct that evades U.S.  sanctions. Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated today . ###

title: Statement from U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent for the World Bank Development Committee and IMF International Monetary and Financial Committee
body: October 14, 2026 This year’s Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank provide an important opportunity to engage on current global economic challenges as well as our work with partners and the international financial institutions to support a pro-growth agenda, macroeconomic and financial stability, and poverty reduction.  We thank Thailand for hosting us for the Annual Meetings. In the United States, President Trump’s America First Investment Policy is promoting robust economic growth and prosperity, fiscal prudence, energy abundance, and regulatory modernization.  Internationally, we are getting back to basics by forging a broad consensus on the need to promote growth as the key condition on which durable prosperity depends.  As G20 President, the United States is focused on promoting strong economic growth, and has prioritized increasing productivity, addressing global imbalances, engaging with the private sector, advancing financial literacy, improving the sovereign debt architecture, and promoting financial sector innovation and regulatory modernization.  When focused on their core missions, the IMF and World Bank are well-placed to help advance these important objectives. The IMF is making progress at getting back to basics.  Through recent policy reviews, the IMF is upgrading its policy toolkit for surveillance and lending and restoring its focus on its core responsibilities.  This includes the external sector issues at the heart of the IMF’s mandate, strengthening surveillance of debt vulnerabilities in low-income countries, and making the financial sector surveillance more risk-based.  Moreover, the IMF has rightly focused on strengthening program design to enhance the effectiveness of IMF-supported reform programs to durably address balance of payments challenges and restore external viability. One area where this refocus must go further is in the IMF’s work on global imbalances.  This especially includes strengthening its analysis and engagement on the role non-market policies and practices and exchange rates play in driving external imbalances.  Policymakers around the world are having difficult discussions about how to sustain market-based systems amid distortionary policies from some economies that skew competition and hurt employment.  The IMF was founded to prevent these kinds of distortive policies and negative spillovers, and must exercise its voice on this critical issue or risk being sidelined. With recent major policy reviews complete, the hard work of implementation begins.  The United States will hold the IMF accountable for translating these reforms into stronger surveillance, more effective lending, and more robust assessment of debt sustainability.  Successfully delivering on the IMF’s core mandate will require commitment from IMF management to be an unflinching truth-teller through surveillance and to hold borrowers accountable in IMF-supported programs.  That same commitment is required of the authorities undertaking painful but necessary macroeconomic adjustments and structural reforms. The IMF must continue to prioritize its work and focus its resources on its core mandate.  New and emerging issues warrant IMF engagement only where they are clearly macrocritical and within the Fund’s mandate, and adding new priorities should require reducing lower-value work, rather than continually expanding the Fund’s agenda such as financing provided through the Resilience and Sustainability Trust that lacks a clear linkage to balance of payments pressures and veers into development-policy lending. The IMF has sufficient resources to accomplish its mission.  The United States remains committed to a strong, quota-based, and adequately resourced IMF, and we continue to work to secure congressional approval for the 16 th General Review of Quotas.  Future quota reviews should be based on resource adequacy needs, as reflected in the recently approved Diriyah Guiding Principles on IMF Quota and Governance Reforms.  Any future quota realignment should reflect members’ relative position in the world economy and be based on a new quota formula. After years of mission creep, the World Bank is beginning to refocus on its core mission of reducing poverty and raising economic growth.  Over the last year, the Bank has strengthened its development agenda by further implementing its jobs initiative, removing inefficient and distortionary climate finance targets, beginning to phase out lending to certain advanced client countries that have not needed Bank support for years, taking steps to better implement its graduation policy, and devising a strategy for supporting a more diversified minerals value chain. These are necessary steps in returning the Bank to its core mission, but significantly more is needed.  The Bank must promote country self-reliance by deploying resources where they are most needed and impactful, graduating more advanced countries from Bank support, delivering better access to reliable, affordable, and abundant energy, and increasing competition and quality in Bank-financed procurement to improve development outcomes.  And, in doing these things, the Bank must be more efficient and selective, pursuing operations with the greatest development impact, rather than simply pushing as much money as possible out the door. We expect the Bank to phase out sovereign lending to countries that have long since met the graduation policy criteria so that the Bank can refocus its resources where they are most needed and impactful.  Despite being long overdue, the planned phase outs of lending to China and Poland represent an important milestone for both countries.  As the Bank continues to implement the graduation policy, we expect to see Graduation Progress Notes that meaningfully assess where graduation-eligible countries fall short of meeting the graduation criteria, and associated Country Partnership Frameworks focusing Bank programming on addressing those shortcomings.  As the Bank enters the longest period in its history without a country graduating from lending eligibility, World Bank Management should take concrete steps to ensure that graduations resume. Similarly, the International Development Association (IDA) must facilitate graduation so that it can focus its resources on the poorest countries where its investments in foundational infrastructure, as well as in reforms that promote debt sustainability and transparency, enhanced domestic resource mobilization, and strong public financial management, help countries develop and stand up to coercive and opaque lending terms from some creditors.  As we discuss IDA’s resources over the next 15 months, IDA must clearly identify its accomplishments in boosting growth, and reducing poverty.  We also support extending the deadline for low-income countries to subscribe to the shares allocated under the 2018 capital increases, helping them preserve and strengthen their representation and voice in the institution. Contributing to country self-reliance also requires the Bank to focus more on the sectors most critical to development and industrialization, chief among them reliable and affordable energy.  Energy abundance sparks economic abundance.  We continue to support the World Bank and African Development Bank goal to extend energy access to 300 million more people in Africa.  Achieving this goal will require the Bank to take a technology-neutral approach rather than restricting borrower choice, including by removing constraints on its support for natural gas and positively responding to borrower demand for gas projects.  Accordingly, the World Bank Group should formally retire its prohibition on financing upstream gas and oil.  The Bank cannot credibly invoke country ownership while categorically excluding upstream projects before their development merits are even assessed. We welcome the recent approval of an IDA project to secure near-term gas supply, prepare mid-and downstream investments, and develop gas strategies in West Africa.  Ultimately, success must be measured by whether countries gain the energy access needed to drive growth, create jobs, and reduce poverty.  We therefore welcome the move to focus on outcomes rather than on arbitrary targets.  To further support energy abundance, the United States is also making an initial contribution to the Nuclear Energy Assistance Trust Fund, which will help countries lay the groundwork for future nuclear energy investments. Critical minerals are foundational inputs to growth and economic security.  We welcome the Bank’s recently approved Metals and Minerals Implementation Plan.  The Bank has an important role to play through policy and regulatory reform, investing in enabling infrastructure and local processing capacity, project finance and de-risking, and strengthening natural resource management.  This includes deep-sea mining, where the Bank can play a catalytic role by providing knowledge and guidance in a nascent sector. Directing resources to countries most in need is not enough; the Bank must position those resources to deliver value.  Procurement policies that reward distortive industrial policies, encourage subsidies, and incentivize corruption and collusion ultimately undermine development, stifle the private sector, and result in higher long-term costs.  The Bank must pursue procurement reforms that result in greater competition and quality.  We recognize recent efforts to expand the use of quality-based procurement approaches, boost the use of local labor, and improve industry outreach, but much of this was necessary just to move closer to the value-for-money objective embodied in the Procurement Framework adopted over a decade ago.  The Bank needs to assess where its current procurement framework, policies, and implementation are still not delivering competition and quality needed for long-term development and adopt further reforms and capacity-building measures to address those shortcomings.  The Bank’s peer institutions are implementing a robust procurement reform agenda.  We expect the World Bank to lead on these efforts rather than fall behind. The International Finance Corporation (IFC) can play an important role in mobilizing private capital to support economic growth and private sector development.  But higher mobilization levels are not a substitute for the harder work of creating markets and crowding in truly private investment in poorer, less creditworthy countries.  We call on the IFC to redouble efforts to meet its 2018 capital increase pledge to make 40 percent of new commitments in the poorest and most fragile countries.  The IFC’s rate of progress towards this commitment has fallen unacceptably short, underscoring the need to align the institution more closely with its core mission. Finally, the IMF and World Bank are ultimately taxpayer-funded public institutions whose budgets should reflect the narrower set of operations that comes with refocusing on their core missions.  We appreciate the flat real administrative budget growth being pursued at both institutions this fiscal year, and expect to see this same approach in future years.  Both institutions and their Governors can and should go further, including by indefinitely freezing – and even reducing – Executive Board budgets and salaries, which now have a combined annual cost over $200 million.  The reduction in the IMF Board’s core budget this year is an important first step in this direction.  The Boards are significantly more expensive, both in overall and per-capita terms, than at other international financial institutions.  Every unnecessary dollar spent on the Boards is a dollar that cannot be used to reduce poverty, promote macroeconomic stability, or  foster growth.  The Bank, Fund, and their members must do more to restrain these inexcusably bloated budgets.  We also call on the IMF to divest from the Bretton Woods Recreation Center and the Concordia Hotel. Streamlining policy priorities will allow both the World Bank and IMF to focus limited public resources on effectively fulfilling their core mandates while responding to crises.  We look forward to working with Management, staff, and other shareholders, to accomplish this task. ###

title: Treasury and IRS Move to Protect Health Care Benefits for Eligible Americans
body: October 14, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement Working Families Tax Cuts Reforms to Prevent Fraud and Abuse of the Premium Tax Credit WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) issued proposed regulations to implement President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), a refundable tax credit that helps eligible American taxpayers afford health insurance purchased through the Health Insurance Exchanges. “Hardworking American taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize health care for people who are ineligible under federal law,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s proposed rules implement the common-sense reforms enacted by the Working Families Tax Cuts to close eligibility loopholes and ensure taxpayer-funded Premium Tax Credits are reserved for eligible Americans. Under President Trump, this Administration is cracking down on fraud and corruption; holding bad actors accountable; lowering health care costs for Americans; and restoring integrity to our tax code and health care system.” “The proposed rules protect eligible taxpayers while strengthening the integrity of the Premium Tax Credit,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “The enhanced verification measures are designed to curb improper claims, ensuring these vital tax benefits go strictly to the hardworking Americans who qualify for them.” “The Trump Administration’s whole-of-government approach to fighting fraud, waste, and abuse is built on the idea that an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz . “Ensuring health programs serve only those who are eligible is one of the most effective ways to protect these programs and the taxpayers who support them. With today’s proposed rules, the Treasury Department is taking another step forward in our collaborative effort to protect taxpayer dollars by shutting down waste and fraud before a single dollar leaves the building.” PROTECTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED BENEFITS FOR ELIGIBLE AMERICANS The proposed rules put the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Premium Tax Credit reforms into effect which strengthen eligibility checks, close gaps in the verification process, and help ensure taxpayer-funded subsidies go only to eligible American taxpayers. The Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud exposed the need for stronger safeguards to protect the integrity of the Federal Marketplace. As part of that work, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced the removal of more than 760,000 unverified “phantom” enrollees from the rolls of the Affordable Care Act (ACA), resulting in $2.2 billion in savings and sending nearly 1 million Americans $500 each who had been overcharged for their Obamacare coverage by the Biden Administration. The Treasury and IRS proposed rules: Strengthen Eligibility Standards: Beginning in 2027, ensures taxpayer-funded health insurance subsidies go only to Americans who qualify under federal law. Protect Taxpayer Benefits for Eligible Americans: Restricts PTC eligibility to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and certain lawfully present noncitizens. Close Verification Gaps: Applies commonsense PTC eligibility checks and adds new verification criteria for any advance PTC payments. The proposed regulations are available here . The changes to Exchange procedures and operations necessary to implement the verification requirements are expected to be addressed in parallel proposed regulations issued by HHS under related provisions of the same statute. ###

title: October 14, 2026 - FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development Effort begins by Soliciting Public Feedback For Immediate Release: October 14, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. As outlined in a new white paper , the Initiative will develop an optimized, fit-for-purpose framework that reflects the realities of rare disease drug development by considering the nuances of each disease, patient needs, product type and the evidence that can be realistically generated in small patient populations. To solicit feedback on the Rare Disease Framework Initiative from patients and disease advocates, industry, and others, the FDA will host an October 28 meeting at the FDA’s White Oak campus. The meeting will be facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA. “Americans with rare diseases cannot afford a regulatory system that treats every condition the same,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Under President Trump, FDA is rethinking rare disease drug development by putting patients at the center and matching regulatory requirements to the realities of small patient populations. We will remove unnecessary barriers, embrace cutting-edge science, and accelerate promising treatments while upholding FDA’s rigorous standards.” “Patients and families living with rare diseases have few or no approved treatment options, and the burden of uncertainty can extend across every part of their lives,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “As we learn more about rare diseases and better understand the breadth of suffering they cause, we must ensure that America’s regulatory system remains at the forefront — prepared to respond to emerging science, anticipate the needs of patients and families, and help bring safe and effective therapies to those who need them. The FDA will fight hard for patients by building a more consistent, predictable, and innovative approach to rare disease drug development while maintaining the rigorous standards Americans expect from the FDA.” The FDA has long used regulatory flexibility and developed targeted programs to support innovation in the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. These efforts have led to meaningful advances for patients and families. Nevertheless, with only 5% or so of rare conditions having an FDA-approved treatment, the FDA agrees with patients, drug developers, and providers that more must be done to speed the development of safe and effective treatments for rare diseases. In developing the framework, the FDA is committed to the following: Providing greater clarity, consistency, and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance and transparent communication. Embedding the patient’s voice both early, and at clearly defined milestones, in the drug development and review process. Further leveraging external expertise to support customization of regulatory review. Building shared resources, robust training, and institutional knowledge on rare disease drug development and review. Applying risk-based approaches, particularly to chemistry, manufacturing, and controls review and pre-approval inspections. Championing the use of cutting-edge science, novel methods and innovative statistical approaches in rare disease drug development. The Initiative is led by the FDA’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, partnering with the Office of the Commissioner, the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. “Patients with rare diseases and their families deserve a regulatory process that addresses the uniqueness of each of their conditions while maintaining the FDA’s rigorous standards,” said the Hub’s Director, Amy Comstock Rick, J.D. “A bold vision to reimagine the framework for rare disease drug development that builds on key learnings and milestones is necessary to meet this moment. This new framework will enhance consistency and predictability for both sponsors and for patients.” Further opportunities to provide input will follow the public meeting, including sector-specific roundtables, Requests for Information, and internal FDA feedback sessions. This feedback will inform the detailed development of a new framework, which might include potential new or revised guidance, revisions to regulations, staff training, and organizational changes. Additional Resources • FDA Rare Disease Innovation Hub • Rare Disease Framework Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: October 14, 2026 - FDA Approves First Treatment for Certain People With BCG-Unresponsive Bladder Cancer
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Treatment for Certain People With BCG-Unresponsive Bladder Cancer Expanded approval of Anktiva marks a new FDA approach to using evidence across closely related forms of bladder cancer For Immediate Release: October 14, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today expanded the approved use of Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln), given with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), to include adults with high-grade papillary-only bladder cancer that has not spread into the bladder muscle and has not responded to BCG treatment. Anktiva is the first FDA-approved treatment specifically for patients with BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only disease. The approval marks a new FDA approach to evaluating treatments for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). The agency based its decision on evidence supporting an earlier approval of Anktiva for adults with another form of NMIBC, carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary tumors, and scientific similarities between CIS and high-grade papillary-only disease. “We listen to patients, clinicians, and researchers, and we act when the science supports a new approach,” said R. Angelo de Claro, M.D., Director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “For Anktiva, our review of the similarities between these cancers allowed us to build on the results in patients with CIS and expand treatment options for people with high-grade papillary tumors alone. This approach may also help guide the development of future treatments.” NMIBC is bladder cancer that has not grown into the bladder’s muscle layer and can include CIS and papillary tumors. CIS forms flat patches along the bladder’s lining, while papillary tumors grow from the lining into the bladder as small, finger-like projections. CIS is always high-grade, while papillary tumors can be low-grade or high-grade. High-grade cancers are more likely to grow and spread than low-grade cancers. Treatment for high-risk NMIBC often starts with BCG, which activates the immune system inside the bladder to fight cancer. Sometimes, however, the cancer persists or returns. Adding Anktiva gives the immune system another way to fight the cancer, and the combination can help some people whose cancer was not controlled by BCG alone. Anktiva’s CIS approval was supported by a trial ( NCT03022825 ) that evaluated the treatment’s effectiveness in 77 adults, some of whom also had papillary tumors. Sixty-two percent achieved a complete response, meaning no high-grade cancer was detected during follow-up assessments, and of those, 58% maintained that response for at least 12 months and 40% for at least 24 months. For today’s expanded approval, the FDA considered these results alongside clinical and laboratory evidence showing that CIS and high-grade papillary tumors share important features. They often occur together, can be difficult to distinguish under a microscope and carry a high risk of returning or progressing when BCG treatment no longer works. These similarities supported applying the evidence of Anktiva’s effectiveness in people with CIS to those with high-grade papillary-only disease. To help developers apply this approach, the FDA is working toward finalizing its draft guidance, “ Bacillus Calmette-Guérin-Unresponsive Nonmuscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Treatment .” The guidance is intended to include discussion of using evidence from studies in patients with CIS to support approval of treatments for BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only NMIBC. Anktiva is given with BCG directly into the bladder through a catheter. It is given once a week for six weeks, with additional treatment based on how the cancer responds. Treatment may continue for up to 37 months. It should be stopped if the cancer persists after a second six-week course, returns or progresses, or side effects become unacceptable. The most common side effects and laboratory abnormalities included painful or frequent urination, an urgent need to urinate, blood in the urine, urinary tract infections, muscle or joint pain, chills, fever, and increased blood levels of creatinine and potassium. Anktiva’s prescribing information warns that delaying surgery to remove all or part of the bladder can allow the cancer to spread to other parts of the body, which can be fatal. The approval was granted to Altor BioScience, LLC. Additional Resources FDA Anktiva Approval Announcement Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. title: Treasury Targets Cartel del Noreste’s Horse Racing Enterprise and Expansive Criminal Network
body: October 13, 2026 Sanctions Disrupt CDN’s Integrated Commercial Operations Supporting Violenceand Cross‑Border Corruption WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 11 entities connected to the U.S.-designated Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) Cartel del Noreste (CDN). Those designated include individuals and businesses involved in quarter horse racing, construction, trucking, and the oil and gas sector, highlighting the cartel’s diverse commercial footprint. CDN’s evolution from its predecessor, Los Zetas—responsible for some of the deadliest mass‑casualty attacks in Mexican history—underscores the severity of CDN’s continued threat to the United States and the region. “Today’s action exposes Cartel del Noreste’s exploitation of the horse racing sector to launder illicit proceeds and finance cartel operations,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “This action marks Treasury’s most significant effort to date to disrupt Cartel del Noreste’s financial infrastructure. Treasury, in close coordination with our law enforcement partners, remains committed to protecting the U.S. financial system from misuse by violent cartels.” CDN’s stronghold sits directly across the border from Laredo, Texas, the busiest port of entry (POE) on the southern border, where nearly 40 percent of all commercial traffic between the United States and Mexico crosses. This deep entrenchment in cross-border industries, combined with CDN’s ability to infiltrate local governments, steer public contracts, and manipulate regional elections, undermines legitimate authority and destabilizes communities on both sides of the border. In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans in close coordination with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025. OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons. Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks. OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, including the U.S. Border Patrol, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, as well as assistance from the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the U.S. Marshals Service. OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC coordinated on this action and previous actions against CDN with the Government of Mexico’s financial intelligence unit, the Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF). The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, E.O.13224, as amended), which targets terrorists and their supporters. This is OFAC’s fourth and largest action to date targeting CDN networks during the Trump Administration. On May 21, 2025, OFAC designated two high-ranking members and arms traffickers of CDN. On August 6, 2025 , OFAC designated three high-ranking members and one associate of CDN, including famous narco-rapper El Makabelico. Earlier this year, on April 14, 2026, OFAC designated three entities and three associates of CDN, including Casino Centenario, a casino just miles from the U.S. border, and Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, criminal advisor to CDN. CARTEL DEL NORESTE Z-40 (left) and Z-42 (right) Based in Mexico directly across from one of the busiest American border crossings, CDN is a violent terrorist cartel founded by the notorious brothers Miguel Angel “Z-40” Trevino Morales and Oscar Omar “Z-42” Trevino Morales. CDN has been involved in the trafficking of narcotics and other illicit drugs, including fentanyl, crystal methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine. CDN, formerly known as Los Zetas, has engaged in horrific violence over the years. This year marks the fifteenth anniversary of the August 25, 2011 deadly Los Zetas arson attack on a casino in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico. This arson attack killed 52 people and injured dozens more, with a majority of those killed being women. This firebombing became one of the deadliest cartel attacks against civilians in Mexican history. Z-40 and Z-42 were arrested by Mexican authorities in 2013 and 2015, respectively, but maintained control over the cartel utilizing corrupt attorneys, including Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, whom OFAC designated in April 2026. The Trevino brothers were transferred from Mexico in February 2025 and are currently facing drug trafficking, racketeering, firearms, and money laundering charges in the District Court for the District of Columbia, with a maximum sentence of life imprisonment. CDN, then known as Los Zetas, was identified by the United States as a specially designated foreign narcotics trafficker on April 15, 2009, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act). On July 24, 2011, Los Zetas was named as a transnational criminal organization (TCO) in the annex to E.O. 13581. On December 15, 2021, OFAC designated CDN pursuant to E.O. 14059. On February 20, 2025, the U.S. Department of State designated CDN as an FTO and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT). AMERICAN QUARTER HORSE RACING – A ZETAS TRADITION FBI raiding an Oklahoma horse farm and Zetas money laundering front in June 2012. CDN has a long history of money laundering through the American Quarter Horse racing industry. Between 2008 and 2012, Z-40 and Z-42 bought and sold racehorses with drug money and trained and raced them in the United States. Over a 30-month period, Zetas-affiliated front persons and shell companies spent $16 million in New Mexico, Oklahoma, California, and Texas to support the operation and laundered upwards of $22 million for the cartel. In June 2012, the U.S. Government seized 455 horses at an Oklahoma horse farm, racing venues, and training farms. Club La Molienda CDN’s involvement in horse racing continues to this day. Club La Molienda ( La Molienda ) is a horse racetrack, restaurant, and bar located on the outskirts of Nuevo Laredo that is controlled by CDN. As the most prominent racetrack in Nuevo Laredo, La Molienda generates revenue for CDN, charging entrance fees for those racing their horses at the track as well as for spectators. CDN leaders and members purchase horses, including many from the United States, to race at La Molienda. La Molienda is controlled by Z-40 but is ultimately overseen by various CDN leaders and associates while Z-40 is incarcerated in the United States. La Molienda on race day. Before a successful bilateral U.S.-Mexico action in April 2026 suspended operations of Casino Centenario, La Molienda and Casino Centenario entered a strategic gambling partnership allowing people to bet on races at La Molienda from the premises of Casino Centenario. In coordination with OFAC’s April 2026 designation of Casino Centenario and related entities, on the same day, Mexico’s UIF took action and the Secretaría de Gobernación suspended the activities of these CDN-linked entities. OFAC designated La Molienda pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN. INSIDE THE WINNER’S CIRCLE – TRACKSIDE ASSOCIATES OF CDN Garza and Elias after winning a race at La Molienda. Gamaliel Garza Garcia ( Garza Garcia ) is a Mexico-based businessman, horse racing enthusiast, and an associate of CDN. Garza Garcia is involved in horse racing in both Mexico and the United States, racing at some of the most prestigious tracks in California and New Mexico. Garza Garcia and his horses frequently race at La Molienda. Garza Garcia’s company, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elias S.A. de C.V. ( CEGESA ), has been utilized by CDN to funnel money to election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates. Additionally, CEGESA has corruptly obtained government contracts and then sub-contracted that work to CDN-affiliated individuals. CEGESA is a major recipient of government contracts in the north of the country, including from the governments of the municipality of Nuevo Laredo and the state of Tamaulipas. Garza Garcia created the Nuevo Laredo-based material supply company Concretos y Productos Asfalticos del Norte, S.A. de C.V. ( COPASA ) to vertically integrate the illicit construction contract scheme. CEGESA performed or subcontracted the work, while COPASA provided the materials. As of early 2026, CEGESA and COPASA were some of the only construction companies authorized by CDN to perform construction work in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. Cuadra San Dibanh Garza Garcia controls Cuadra San Dibanh , an Anahuac, Nuevo Leon-based Quarter Horse racing barn. Cuadra San Dibanh frequently races at La Molienda and other major racetracks throughout Mexico. Garza Garcia also owns and controls an extensive corporate network of construction and fuel companies in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. This includes the following six companies, all based in Nuevo Laredo: Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V. , a construction company; Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V. , a construction company; Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V. , a fuel and gas company; Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V. , a fuel and gas company; Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V. , a fuel and gas company; and Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V. , a fuel and gas transportation company. Gamaliel Garza Elias ( Garza Elias ), Garza Garcia’s son, is being designated for his role in CEGESA, where he is involved in the day-to-day operations of CEGESA. Garza Elias has also delivered cash to fund election campaigns for CDN’s preferred political candidates in Mexico. OFAC designated Garza Garcia pursuant to E.O. 14059, for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, CDN. Garza Garcia is also being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, CDN. OFAC designated CEGESA; COPASA; Cuadra San Dibanh; Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V.; Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V.; Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V.; Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V.; Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V.; and Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V. pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Garza Garcia. OFAC designated Garza Elias pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended,for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CEGESA. OTHER PLAYERS IN THE NUEVO LAREDO PLAZA Pablo Cesar Guajardo Alvarez ( Guajardo ), known as “Takia,” is a current CDN plaza boss of Nuevo Laredo and former leader of CDN’s sicarios. Plaza bosses are in charge of all cartel activity in their area of responsibility. Guajardo was arrested in 2020 for his connection to the January 4, 2017 assassination of Ricardo Martinez Chavez and four public servants, but has since been released. Guajardo has been involved in arms trafficking on behalf of CDN. OFAC designated Guajardo pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN. Tamex Leasing or Tamex Logistics ( Tamex ) is a Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas-based trucking company involved in the smuggling of narcotics into the United States. Tamex’s truckyard in Nuevo Laredo has been the originator of at least two cocaine shipments bound for the United States. Seized by law enforcement, these shipments were stored in hidden compartments of the trailers’ brake drums and totaled 52 kilograms. Francisco Javier Inzunza Partida ( Inzunza ) is a dispatcher for Tamex who was involved in dispatching the two trailers seized for concealed narcotics. OFAC designated Tamex and Inzunza pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions. In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions. OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List .
